subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual group activation as core channel behavior, or should maintainers first define a generic passive-observation/plugin API seam and keep the contextual decision policy in a plugin?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the right boundary controls privacy, provider exposure, config surface, channel delivery semantics, and ClawHub/plugin ownership; automation cannot choose that product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Design plugin/API seam first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad product discussion, advance a narrow passive-observation hook/API such as the inbound_observed direction, and implement contextual policy outside core when the seam is sufficient.

options.title: Approve core opt-in mode
options.body: Sponsor a core implementation only after maintainers define the opt-in config, provider fallback rules, log retention/redaction, channel coverage, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep current mention/always behavior and close or postpone contextual activation until there is stronger maintainer demand for LLM-mediated ambient group listening.

recommendation.title: Design plugin/API seam first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad product discussion, advance a narrow passive-observation hook/API such as the inbound_observed direction, and implement contextual policy outside core when the seam is sufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged recent Telegram group mention behavior changes and is the strongest available routing candidate for a cross-channel product/security boundary choice.
